target.title: feat(exec): deny-over-allow exec approval denylist (#6615)
target.body:
Fixes #6615. Supersedes #92456 (author inactive since 2026-06-12, no response to review, conflicts with main — full credit to @Hidetsugu55 for the STOP-list concept and dual-host enforcement approach, both kept here).

## Update — re-review 2 (clawsweeper P1 blockers resolved)

The previous review's three P1 blockers were "contract declared but not wired." All three are now wired end-to-end, with focused tests on each exact path plus refreshed real-behavior proof. Also merged latest `origin/main` (resolves the CONFLICTING/behind-main note).

- **[P1] Wire `tools.exec.denylist` into config schema + gateway caller** — `denylist` added to the strict zod `ToolExecBaseShape` (`src/config/zod-schema.agent-runtime.ts`, non-empty-pattern refinement) so `openclaw config validate` accepts it and rejects malformed entries; threaded as `execConfigDenylist` through `agent-tools.ts` → `bash-tools.exec.ts` → `processGatewayAllowlist`, unioned across global + per-agent layers (`resolveEffectiveExecDenylist`). Tests: `config.schema-regressions.test.ts`, `bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts`.
- **[P1] Pass denylist hits into node-host `system.run`** — `invoke-system-run.ts` now evaluates the effective denylist (openclaw.json global + per-agent + `exec-approvals.json` file layer) and passes `denylisted`/`denylistReason` into `evaluateSystemRunPolicy`; the model auto-reviewer is hard-blocked on a hit (human-only), and unanalyzable commands fail closed. Tests: `invoke-system-run.test.ts` (+ node denial reason `denylist-hit`).
- **[P1] Add denylist to exec-approval protocol writes** — `ExecApprovalsDenylistEntrySchema` + `denylist` added to `ExecApprovalsPolicyFields` in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/schema/exec-approvals.ts` so `exec.approvals.set` / `exec.approvals.node.set` round-trip the field. Tests: `exec-approvals-validators.test.ts`.

Two extra hardening changes made while wiring the above:

- **Real defect fix:** `sanitizeExecApprovalPolicy` (`src/infra/exec-approvals.ts`) was silently dropping the defaults-layer `denylist` on every `saveExecApprovals` write — a routine policy write would disarm an operator's STOP list. Now normalized and preserved.
- **Standalone gate:** the gateway host now has an independent `requiresDenylistApproval || …` short-circuit in `processGatewayAllowlist`, so the deny-over-allow guarantee cannot regress even if `requiresExecApproval`'s denylist handling ever changes.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's exec approvals support allowlists but no denylist: there is no way to force human approval (or denial) for specific dangerous commands when an agent runs at `security=full` / `ask=off`, or when a broad allowlist/durable trust would otherwise auto-approve them. #6615 asks for a deny-over-allow screening layer so commands like `git push --force` or `rm -rf` patterns always require an explicit human decision, regardless of permissive settings.

## Fix

- `src/infra/exec-approvals-denylist.ts`: entry normalization, strict validation (`collectExecDenylistErrors`), and `resolveEffectiveExecDenylist` (de-duplicated union across layers — deny anywhere = deny).
- **Both config layers**: `openclaw.json` `tools.exec.denylist` (global + per-agent) **and** `~/.openclaw/exec-approvals.json` (defaults + `*` + agent), wired through both exec hosts (see Update above).
- **Shared pattern language**: denylist patterns reuse the existing allowlist glob compiler via a new `matchesExecGlob` export — no second matcher to keep in sync (`*` → `[^/]*`, `**` → `.*`, `?` → `[^/]`).
- **Deny wins first**: a hit forces approval ahead of `ask=off`, `security=full`, allowlist hits, and durable allow-always trust, on both the gateway exec host and node-host `system.run` (node denial reason `denylist-hit`). Explicit allow-once approval still clears a hit; `security=deny` still wins overall.
- Conservative fallback: unanalyzable command + configured denylist ⇒ approval required, not fail-open. Basename variants and `bash -c "..."` inner payloads are screened.

## Evidence

**Typecheck (repo's real TS-Go checker):** `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:core:test` both clean on this branch. (Stock `tsc` throws a bogus TS4058 in `src/secrets/config-io.ts` that tsgo does not — pre-existing on `main`.)

**Focused tests — all green on the exact paths flagged:**
- `src/infra/exec-approvals-denylist.test.ts` — 19 (normalize/dedupe, both-layer union, exact/glob/basename/wrapper matches, conservative fallback, precedence).
- `src/node-host/exec-policy.test.ts` — 19 and `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.test.ts` — 36 (node-host `system.run` enforcement, config-layer union, human-only, `denylist-hit`).
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts` — 54 (gateway standalone denylist gate at `security=full`/`ask=off`).
- `packages/gateway-protocol/src/exec-approvals-validators.test.ts` — 8 (protocol/file denylist round-trip).
- `src/config/config.schema-regressions.test.ts` — 39 and `src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts` — 23 (config schema accept/validate + label/help coverage).

> Note: on a host that symlinks `head` to cargo-coreutils, one unrelated pre-existing test (`processGatewayAllowlist > uses a plan-backed enforced command…`) fails on a `/usr/bin/head` vs `/usr/lib/cargo/bin/coreutils/head` path assertion. It is environmental and independent of this PR (our diff to that test file is additive only).

**Real behavior proof** (real decision code path via `node --import tsx`, no test doubles — `git push --force origin main` allowlisted + durable-trusted at `security=full`/`ask=off`, denylist supplied through the openclaw.json config layer exactly as the wired callers do):

```
## BEFORE (control: no denylist configured)
[gateway-host] command="git push --force origin main" security=full ask=off allowlisted=true durable=true -> AUTO-RUN
[node-host]    command="git push --force origin main" -> ALLOWED

## AFTER (denylist configured via openclaw.json tools.exec.denylist)
denylist = [{"pattern":"git push*--force*","reason":"history rewrite"}]
[gateway-host] -> APPROVAL REQUIRED
[node-host]    -> DENIED (denylist-hit)

## AFTER + explicit allow-once approval
[node-host]    -> ALLOWED (approval cleared the hit)
```

## Scope notes

- Contract is now complete across config schema, gateway protocol write schema, gateway host caller, node-host `system.run`, docs/help (`schema.help.ts` + `schema.labels.ts`), tests, and real proof.
- No drive-by refactors.


## Node-host prompt parity (b0164f0fe8a, 2026-07-09)

Review found that the `host=node` `security=full`/`ask=off` fast path invoked `system.run` directly before prepare/approval registration, so a denylist STOP rule hard-denied server-side (`denylist-hit`) instead of raising the documented human allow-once prompt.

Fixed for prompt parity (recommended option):

- The direct fast path is taken only when the caller-visible effective denylist is **known empty**: the `openclaw.json` config layer is empty AND the node approvals-file denylist (fetched via `exec.approvals.node.get`) is known and empty. Fetch failures fail **closed** into the prepare path.
- On the prepare path, the effective denylist (config layer + node approvals-file layer) is evaluated caller-side; a hit forces a registered human approval request even at full/off, mirroring the gateway host: auto-review is excluded (human-only), and `allow-always` is downgraded to one-shot so no durable trust can be minted from a denylist hit.
- Non-matching commands with a configured denylist still auto-run (via the prepare path); setups with no denylist keep the direct fast path.

Focused tests added in `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts`: config-layer hit registers an approval request (no direct denial), approvals-file hit registers an approval request, non-matching denylist auto-runs, known-empty denylist keeps the fast path, approvals fetch failure fails closed to prepare. `vitest run src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts src/infra/exec-approvals-denylist.test.ts src/node-host/exec-policy.test.ts --pool=forks` => 4 files, 146 tests passed; tsgo typecheck clean.

Honest proof status: production decision-function proof and the focused node-host approval-registration tests are in; a live gateway+node prompt -> allow-once -> runs-exactly-once capture is being prepared on a dedicated QA host and will be appended when complete.

Known residual (intentional, documented here): a denylist configured ONLY in the node machine's own local `openclaw.json` remains invisible to the gateway-side caller and still hard-denies server-side (fail-closed). The two operator surfaces this PR documents (`tools.exec.denylist` config layer and the exec-approvals file) now both get prompt parity on host=node.

target.title: fix(agents): CJK-aware tool-result truncation budgets
target.body:
Closes #103847

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users with CJK-heavy tool results (Chinese, Japanese, Korean text) would keep oversized tool payloads in the agent context even though those results already consumed far more tokens than the live truncation budget intended. Dense CJK was measured by raw UTF-16 length while the budget assumed ~4 Latin characters per token, so content could under-count by up to ~4× and skip truncation.

## Why This Change Was Made

Split live tool-result budgets into two units:

1. **Estimated / token-share** (`maxTokens * 4`) — compared with CJK-aware `estimateStringChars` so dense CJK triggers truncation at the intended token share.
2. **Physical UTF-16 ceiling** — configured `toolResultMaxChars` and the auto hard-cap ladder stay physical-character contracts (not re-interpreted as estimated chars).

When truncating multi-block results, convert each block’s estimated share back to a physical UTF-16 slice budget, clamp `minKeep` to that adjusted allocation (so small caps cannot retain more estimated cost than budgeted), keep short sibling marker blocks intact, and skip empty text blocks so inflation ratios never become NaN. Runtime paths (`run` / `attempt` / session tool-result guard) pass dual budgets via `resolveLiveToolResultBudgets`.

## User Impact

- CJK-heavy tool sessions truncate at the intended context share instead of retaining near-full CJK payloads that pressure the model window.
- Existing `toolResultMaxChars` config remains a **physical** character ceiling (upgrade-compatible).
- Pure ASCII behavior stays the same under the dual-budget path.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS (Crabbox bypass)

Head: `b30d7c138` (`fix(agents): charge intact siblings in dual-budget truncation`)

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.test.ts \
  src/utils/cjk-chars.test.ts \
  src/agents/session-tool-result-guard.test.ts
# agents: 72/72 (tool-result-truncation, including dual-budget / minKeep / config ceiling cases)
# unit-fast: 18/18 (cjk-chars) + 35/35 (session-tool-result-guard)
```

Focused cases added/updated for ClawSweeper unit-boundary findings:

- configured physical ceiling not treated as estimated (CJK keep > ~config/4)
- full CJK payload kept when estimated budget is loose and physical config allows
- small-cap CJK clamps `minKeep` to adjusted physical allocation
- `resolveLiveToolResultBudgets` separates estimated token-share vs physical config

Main-contrast measurement (16000 estimated-char token-share budget):

```json
{
  "ascii_physical": 8000,
  "ascii_estimated": 8000,
  "cjk_physical": 8000,
  "cjk_estimated": 32000,
  "cjk_would_truncate_main": false,
  "cjk_would_truncate_fixed": true
}
```

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Live tool-result truncation weights dense CJK for automatic token-share budgets while preserving configured physical character ceilings; min-keep no longer defeats CJK-adjusted physical allocations under small caps.
- Environment: local macOS openclaw checkout on branch `fix/103847-cjk-tool-result-truncation` @ `879763fc08a9`, Node + `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs`.
- Current-main contrast: On main, `getToolResultTextLength` sums `text.length`, so 8000 CJK chars measure as 8000 against a 16000 estimated-char cap and are **not** truncated despite ~token-share overshoot. After this patch the same content measures as 32000 estimated chars and is truncated under the token-share path. Configured `toolResultMaxChars: 8000` remains a physical ceiling (dual budgets), not an estimated-char reinterpretation.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  1. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.test.ts`
  2. `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/session-tool-result-guard.test.ts src/utils/cjk-chars.test.ts`
- Evidence after fix: 72/72 + 35/35 + 18/18 green; dual-budget and minKeep regressions assert ClawSweeper P1/P2 unit boundaries.
- Control check: Existing ASCII truncation, aggregate recovery, projection, and head/tail strategy tests still pass.
- Observed result after fix: CJK auto path truncates; physical config ceiling preserved; small-cap minKeep clamped.
- ClawSweeper P1 follow-up (`b30d7c138`): intact short ASCII siblings reserved against both dual budgets before dense CJK truncation; mixed-block unit regression + allocator math show composed next-request-visible estimated chars stay ≤ token-share budget (~15935 / 16000).
- What was not tested: Live multi-turn embedded agent run against a real provider with production CJK tool output (provider transcript redaction); non-macOS hosts; full rebase onto latest main (additive-only push).

## Follow-up to ClawSweeper review

Addressed on `b30d7c138` (on top of prior dual-budget work):

1. **P1** Charge preserved/intact sibling blocks against shared dual budgets — reserve estimated + physical capacity for short intact markers first, then distribute only remaining budgets to truncatable siblings (`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/tool-result-truncation.ts`).
2. Mixed short-ASCII + dense-CJK regression asserts the completed multi-block tool result stays within the estimated token-share cap while keeping the marker intact.
3. Focused proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs` tool-result-truncation **73/73**, cjk-chars **18/18**, session-tool-result-guard **35/35**.

Allocator measurement (short ASCII marker + 8000 CJK under estimated 16000 / physical 64000):

```json
{
  "case": "short_ascii_sibling_plus_dense_cjk_allocator_math",
  "estimatedBudget": 16000,
  "physicalBudget": 64000,
  "marker_intact": true,
  "marker_physical": 26,
  "marker_estimated": 26,
  "cjk_original_physical": 8000,
  "cjk_physical_budget_after_reserve": 3993,
  "total_estimated_after_approx": 15935,
  "within_estimated_budget": true,
  "next_request_visible_estimated_chars_approx": 15935
}
```

Requesting re-review.

This fix was implemented with AI assistance (Grok). Human review of the diff, tests, and proof is still expected before merge.

target.title: fix(discord): stop retrying non-idempotent sends on post-connect-ambiguous errors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Discord message creates can complete at Discord while the client receives a transport failure. Retrying the same non-idempotent create without a server deduplication key can deliver a duplicate message.

## Why This Change Was Made

Each direct Discord Create Message now receives a 24-character random nonce with `enforce_nonce: true`. The nonce is built once before the retry runner, so a retry returns the existing message rather than creating another. This covers text, media, components, stickers, polls, approvals, and voice messages.

The nonce-protected Create Message classifier keeps pre-connect failures, rate limits, and HTTP 502 retryable. Forum and media thread creation use the pre-connect-only classifier because Discord documents nonce enforcement only for Create Message, not the endpoint that creates a thread and starter message together.

## Why this is the right boundary

The retry module still owns retry classification. Message construction owns the create nonce, which remains stable for all attempts of one logical create. Forum thread creation selects the narrower retry policy at its endpoint boundary. Idempotent REST operations retain the broad transient retry policy unchanged.

## Verification

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/retry.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.message-request.test.ts extensions/discord/src/send.creates-thread.test.ts extensions/discord/src/outbound-payload.contract.test.ts extensions/discord/src/client.test.ts extensions/discord/src/outbound-adapter.test.ts` passed with 136 assertions.
- Scoped `tsgo`, `oxlint`, and `oxfmt --check` passed for the changed paths.
- Structured closeout review completed with no actionable findings.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: a retried HTTP 502 on a sticker or poll create sent a fresh nonce on the second attempt, so Discord could not deduplicate the create and delivered a duplicate message.
Real environment tested: the production `sendStickerDiscord` and `sendPollDiscord` paths driven end to end through `createChannelMessage`, the Discord retry runner, and `createDiscordMessageNonce`, with only the Discord REST `post` boundary substituted to return HTTP 502 then HTTP 200 on identical inputs; run on the pre-fix tree cb1642f798 where the create body is built inside the retry callback, and on this patch head 9a58f89a6f where the create body is built once before the retry runner.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: drive `sendStickerDiscord("channel:789", ["123"], { content: "hiya", retry: { attempts: 2 } })` and `sendPollDiscord("channel:789", { question, options }, { retry: { attempts: 2 } })` where the first Discord POST rejects with status 502 and the second resolves, then read the nonce carried on each recorded POST body.
Evidence after fix:
```
# BEFORE (pre-fix tree cb1642f798, sticker/poll body built inside the retry callback)
sticker create, upstream returns 502 then 200: POST attempts=2 | nonce attempt 1=51b6b881e0d78390c74ee04b | nonce attempt 2=ffd94920965564c647ed9413 | nonce identical across attempts=false
poll create, upstream returns 502 then 200: POST attempts=2 | nonce attempt 1=b5a6300e54a3b414fc1471b7 | nonce attempt 2=978a37c0dfdc8f45460d9e2a | nonce identical across attempts=false

# AFTER (this patch, head 9a58f89a6f, identical 502-then-200 sequence)
sticker create, upstream returns 502 then 200: POST attempts=2 | nonce attempt 1=c15fe9cc6af86ec91672dacc | nonce attempt 2=c15fe9cc6af86ec91672dacc | nonce identical across attempts=true
poll create, upstream returns 502 then 200: POST attempts=2 | nonce attempt 1=6cdf7a07ee99c8e0705e31f9 | nonce attempt 2=6cdf7a07ee99c8e0705e31f9 | nonce identical across attempts=true
```
Observed result after fix: the second attempt carries the exact same nonce as the first for both sticker and poll, so Discord `enforce_nonce` collapses the retried create back to the original message instead of delivering a second one; before the patch each attempt carried a different nonce and the retry created a duplicate.

Live Discord server-side deduplication (real API): the client-side result above establishes that the fix makes a retried create reuse one nonce. The server half was then verified directly against the live Discord REST API (`discord.com/api/v10`) with a real bot in a real guild, sending Create Message with `enforce_nonce: true`. This exercises the actual Discord dedup behavior, not a substituted boundary. Bot, guild, channel, and message ids are masked.
```
# AFTER (fix behavior): retry reuses one nonce -> Discord dedups
same-nonce create x2 (nonce 7b55...ef5): POST #1 -> 200 id 1525...284 | POST #2 -> 200 id 1525...284 (same id: true) | messages delivered = 1

# BEFORE (bug behavior): per-attempt nonce -> Discord treats as two creates
per-attempt-nonce create x2 (nonces a4a4...77f , 3499...3b1): POST #1 -> 200 id 1525...460 | POST #2 -> 200 id 1525...940 (distinct id: true) | messages delivered = 2
```
Observed result (live): sending the identical nonce twice makes Discord return the same message id on both calls and deliver exactly one message; sending a fresh nonce per attempt delivers two messages. This confirms the fix prevents duplicate delivery at the Discord server, and reproduces the duplicate under the pre-fix per-attempt-nonce behavior. Probe messages were deleted after the run.
What was not tested: the forum and media thread pre-connect classifier path was not re-driven in this run; retry-schedule windows longer than Discord's unspecified nonce-retention period were not exercised.

target.title: fix(codex): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox process execution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`runProcess()` in the sandbox exec server listens on `child.stdout.on("data")` and `child.stderr.on("data")` but does not register `child.stdout.on("error")` / `child.stderr.on("error")` handlers. Node.js does not forward pipe stream errors to `child.on("error")` — an unhandled `error` event on a readable stream crashes the process with `ERR_UNHANDLED_ERROR`. A broken sandbox stdout/stderr pipe takes down the codex sandbox exec server.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **`child.stdout.on("error")`**: preserve the failure message and kill the child with `SIGTERM`. Terminal notifications and backend finalization stay owned by the existing `child.once("close")` handler, so the process is never reported closed while the child is still running.
- **`child.stderr.on("error")`**: stderr is diagnostic-only; a broken stderr pipe must not kill a healthy process — logged via `embeddedAgentLog.warn`.

## User Impact

A broken sandbox stdout/stderr pipe no longer crashes the exec server. Stdout failures terminate the managed process through the normal close lifecycle; stderr failures are logged without disrupting execution.

## Evidence

**Realistic-stream regression** (`processes.stream-errors.test.ts`): `spawn` is mocked to return a child whose `stdout`/`stderr`/`stdin` are real `PassThrough` streams, driven through the production `startProcess` entry point. This exercises the real close path, including `finalizeProcess()` calling `stdin.destroy()` and `finalizeExec`.

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/processes.stream-errors.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  2 passed (2)
```

**What the tests assert (after fix):**

1. **Stdout error → kill, then finalize via close:**
   - `managed.failure` is set; `child.kill("SIGTERM")` is called; `managed.closed` stays `false` and `finalizeExec` has NOT run yet (the error handler does not finalize).
   - After the real `close` event: `managed.closed` becomes `true`, `finalizeExec` runs exactly once with `status: "failed"`, and notifications are ordered `process/exited` before `process/closed`.
2. **Stderr error → warn only:** `embeddedAgentLog.warn` is called, `child.kill` is never called, the process stays alive, and `finalizeExec` does not run.

**Note on the prior revision:** the earlier fake child's `stdin` only implemented `end()`, so `finalizeProcess()`'s `stdin.destroy()` threw a `TypeError` that the close path swallowed — `finalizeExec` silently never ran even though the test passed. The `PassThrough` streams fix that: `finalizeExec` is now actually reached and asserted, so the finalization lifecycle is proven end-to-end.

**Static checks:** `oxlint` — exit 0; `oxfmt --check` — clean.

**What was not tested:** a live OS-level pipe failure (requires resource exhaustion). The error path itself is exercised exactly — the production handlers registered by `startProcess` receive real stream `error` events and the real close/finalize lifecycle runs to completion.

## Regression Test Plan

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/processes.stream-errors.test.ts` — 2/2 passed
- `oxlint` — exit 0; `oxfmt --check` — clean

AI-assisted.

target.title: fix(sessions): prevent maintenance from deleting active sessions
target.body:
Closes #102064

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where scheduled agent work could lose its session state and final delivery when automatic session maintenance pruned or archived the session while the run was still active.

## Why This Change Was Made

target.title: fix(cron): publish removals after durable commit
target.body:
Fixes #104078.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where external cron mirrors could observe a one-shot job as removed before OpenClaw had durably committed that deletion. If the final store write failed, the observer could cancel a wake for a job that still existed on disk, while the live Gateway could temporarily expose the speculative deletion.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Buffer automatic `removed` events for manual runs, normal timer runs, and startup catch-up until the final durable write succeeds.
- Restore the complete live cron topology, durable next-wake snapshot, and catch-up deferral ownership when that write fails.
- Keep the completed deleted-job snapshot for the eventual event, and remove an unreachable invalid-persisted-job deletion branch.
- Document `scheduled` and `removed` hook events as post-commit reconciliation hints.

The change preserves existing `started` and `finished` timing. It does not turn lifecycle hooks into an ordered delta stream; consumers should still reconcile the full durable cron view.

## User Impact

Plugin authors and host integrations can now treat `cron_changed` removal notifications as durable deletion facts. A failed cron-store write emits no removal, and subsequent cron reads continue to expose the still-durable job.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kx7fqgk4tjw6e9zw6dar21gs`: six new manual, timer, and startup-catch-up success/failure regressions passed.

target.title: fix(googlechat): add 30s request timeout to Google OAuth fetch factory
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`createGoogleAuthFetch()` is the shared factory for all Google OAuth HTTP requests in the Google Chat plugin. It calls `fetchWithSsrFGuard` without a `timeoutMs` deadline. A Google OAuth endpoint that accepts the TCP connection but never sends response headers can hang all Google Chat authentication indefinitely, blocking token exchange, credential refresh, and certificate fetch.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added `GOOGLE_AUTH_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` applied to the single `fetchWithSsrFGuard` call inside `createGoogleAuthFetch()`. This protects every Google OAuth operation with one shared deadline.

30s matches the established REST API timeout convention (mattermost `MATTERMOST_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`, msteams `GRAPH_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS`, googlechat/api.ts `GOOGLECHAT_API_TIMEOUT_MS`, etc.).

## User Impact

A stalled Google OAuth endpoint no longer hangs the plugin indefinitely. All auth operations fail with a timeout-class error after 30s instead of waiting forever.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested:** Node v24, local OpenClaw checkout, PR head commit.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/googlechat/src/google-auth.runtime.test.ts --run

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  19 passed (19)
```

```
npx oxlint extensions/googlechat/src/google-auth.runtime.ts
# exit 0

git diff upstream/main --stat
# 2 files changed, 5 insertions(+)
```

**Observed result after fix:** `createGoogleAuthFetch()` now carries a 30s deadline via `fetchWithSsrFGuard.timeoutMs`. All Google OAuth operations (token exchange, credential refresh, certificate fetch) route through this single factory. Test assertions confirm the `timeoutMs` field is present in every guarded fetch call.

**What was not tested:** A live Google OAuth endpoint; the hang behavior requires the server to accept the connection without responding, reproduced in sibling PRs with real loopback HTTP servers.

## Regression Test Plan

- `npx oxlint extensions/googlechat/src/google-auth.runtime.ts` — **exit 0**
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/googlechat/src/google-auth.runtime.test.ts --run` — **19 passed**
- `git diff upstream/main --stat` — **2 files, +5/-0**

## Root Cause

`createGoogleAuthFetch()` calls `fetchWithSsrFGuard` without a `timeoutMs` — if the Google OAuth endpoint accepts the connection but never sends response headers, the promise never settles and all Google Chat authentication is blocked. Fix: add `GOOGLE_AUTH_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000` at the single chokepoint.

Closes #104058

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `scripts/clawlog.sh` printed the full usage help when invoked with no arguments, even though its own help text documents `clawlog` (no options) as "Show last 50 lines from past 5 minutes (default)."

It also fixes a secondary issue where options that require a value (`-n`, `-l`, `-c`, `-s`, `-o`) crashed with an unbound-variable error when the value was omitted, instead of printing a clear error.

target.title: feat: add readiness conditions and hosting profiles
target.body:
Related RFC: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/33  ## What Problem This Solves  OpenClaw exposes Gateway `/ready` and `/readyz`, but the current fixed evaluator cannot express whether a selected runtime posture is actually usable, let plugins contribute bounded observational evidence, or give operators one structured condition model across HTTP, health, status, and CLI surfaces.  This leaves container and platform hosts maintaining private checks for failures such as loopback-only container listeners, full workspaces, unavailable controlled nodes, and required external plugin dependencies.  ## Why This Change Was Made  This draft adds one canonical readiness-condition model and a small catalog of standard, release-testable hosting profiles:  | Profile | Runtime posture | Additional required evidence | | --- | --- | --- | | `local` | Default local or foreground Gateway | Config, writable workspace, and Gateway lifecycle evidence | | `container` | Gateway directly reachable through a container listener | Effective listener is non-loopback | | `reverse-proxy` | Gateway behind a trusted identity proxy | Trusted-proxy auth header and trusted source | | `node-mode` | Gateway controlling execution targets | Pairing, live target, command approval, and control channel |  Existing startup, drain, selected-channel, suppressed-channel, and event-loop observations become iterable required or advisory conditions while legacy response fields remain compatibility projections. Required `False` or `Unknown` conditions fail readiness; advisory findings remain visible without changing readiness success.  Plugins can register namespaced, self-describing readiness criteria through the existing activation-scoped registry. Plugin criteria are advisory by default. An operator profile may extend one standard profile and promote selected criteria to required, but cannot remove or weaken inherited conditions.  `openclaw ready` is a thin projection of the authoritative live Gateway result. Human output lists structured findings; `--json` preserves the canonical successful result; exit status fails closed for required failures, unknowns, transport errors, or a missing readiness contract.  ## User Impact  Existing installations select `local` when no profile is configured. Operators can select a profile through `hosting.profile`, `OPENCLAW_HOSTING_PROFILE`, or `gateway run --hosting-profile`, then use the existing `/readyz` endpoint or:  ```bash openclaw ready openclaw ready --json ```  Profiles validate effective runtime state; they do not generate or repair configuration. Docker, Kubernetes, systemd, OCC, and other hosts continue to own probe timing, retries, provisioning, placement, and policy rollout.  ## Review Slices  The consolidated branch contains the complete implementation. These stacked fork PRs preserve smaller review boundaries and focused evidence:  - [PR 17: core conditions and local profile](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/17) - [PR 18: standard profile selection](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/18) - [PR 19: node-mode readiness](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/19) - [PR 22: workspace writability](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/22) - [PR 23: readiness providers and operator profiles](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/23) - [PR 27: canonical ready CLI](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/27)  [PR 21](https://github.com/giodl73-repo/openclaw/pull/21), which makes the packaged profile lane release-blocking, is intentionally excluded. That governance change should follow contract acceptance and successful packaged Docker proof.  ## Evidence  - Final composed readiness/Gateway/status/package-planning run: 196 assertions passed. - Ready CLI and production command registration: 49 assertions passed after current-head review fixes. - Docker scenario planner: 33 assertions passed. - Focused formatting, lint, docs listing, and diff checks passed on the sliced heads. - Current-head Codex review: PR 23 clean against PR 22; PR 27 clean against PR 23 after fixing lazy registration and best-effort config loading.  The package-installed `test:docker:hosting-profiles` lane is included but is not wired into the blocking release workflow. The complete packaged Docker lane passes on sanitized AWS Crabbox at the exact PR head.  ## Boundaries  This PR does not add Lobster, Scout, Microsoft, tenant, OCC-resource, or AgentHarness protocol concepts. It does not add policy or doctor dependencies, generate config, define host probe timing, or route agent traffic through a control plane.   ## Packaged Docker Proof

Exact head `153d413b25cefa8b44978ff16bece0604863d9af` passed the complete package-installed hosting-profile lane on sanitized AWS Crabbox:

- Provider: `aws`
- Run: `run_578659dd34be`
- Lease: `cbx_221b83795d90` (`swift-krill`)
- Machine: `c7a.8xlarge`, Linux
- Command: `pnpm test:docker:hosting-profiles`
- Result: exit `0`; lease stopped
- Security boundary: trusted-main wrapper, `--fresh-pr`, exact-head verification, no IAM role, public network, no Tailscale, no credential hydration

Validated scenarios:

- local ready
- container ready and loopback fail-closed
- reverse-proxy ready and missing-auth fail-closed
- node-mode unpaired fail-closed and paired/approved node ready
- workspace storage-full fail-closed and recovery to ready

The first complete runtime attempt exposed that the harness auto-approved device authentication but never approved the separate node command pairing. Commit `153d413b25c` adds that explicit operator approval step; the exact-head rerun passed.

target.title: fix(codex): handle stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox process execution
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`runProcess()` in the sandbox exec server listens on `child.stdout.on("data")` and `child.stderr.on("data")` but does not register `child.stdout.on("error")` / `child.stderr.on("error")` handlers. Node.js does not forward pipe stream errors to `child.on("error")` — an unhandled `error` event on a readable stream crashes the process with `ERR_UNHANDLED_ERROR`. A broken sandbox stdout/stderr pipe takes down the codex sandbox exec server.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **`child.stdout.on("error")`**: preserve the failure message and kill the child with `SIGTERM`. Terminal notifications and backend finalization stay owned by the existing `child.once("close")` handler, so the process is never reported closed while the child is still running.
- **`child.stderr.on("error")`**: stderr is diagnostic-only; a broken stderr pipe must not kill a healthy process — logged via `embeddedAgentLog.warn`.

## User Impact

A broken sandbox stdout/stderr pipe no longer crashes the exec server. Stdout failures terminate the managed process through the normal close lifecycle; stderr failures are logged without disrupting execution.

## Evidence

**Realistic-stream regression** (`processes.stream-errors.test.ts`): `spawn` is mocked to return a child whose `stdout`/`stderr`/`stdin` are real `PassThrough` streams, driven through the production `startProcess` entry point. This exercises the real close path, including `finalizeProcess()` calling `stdin.destroy()` and `finalizeExec`.

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/processes.stream-errors.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
     Tests  2 passed (2)
```

**What the tests assert (after fix):**

1. **Stdout error → kill, then finalize via close:**
   - `managed.failure` is set; `child.kill("SIGTERM")` is called; `managed.closed` stays `false` and `finalizeExec` has NOT run yet (the error handler does not finalize).
   - After the real `close` event: `managed.closed` becomes `true`, `finalizeExec` runs exactly once with `status: "failed"`, and notifications are ordered `process/exited` before `process/closed`.
2. **Stderr error → warn only:** `embeddedAgentLog.warn` is called, `child.kill` is never called, the process stays alive, and `finalizeExec` does not run.

**Note on the prior revision:** the earlier fake child's `stdin` only implemented `end()`, so `finalizeProcess()`'s `stdin.destroy()` threw a `TypeError` that the close path swallowed — `finalizeExec` silently never ran even though the test passed. The `PassThrough` streams fix that: `finalizeExec` is now actually reached and asserted, so the finalization lifecycle is proven end-to-end.

**Static checks:** `oxlint` — exit 0; `oxfmt --check` — clean.

**What was not tested:** a live OS-level pipe failure (requires resource exhaustion). The error path itself is exercised exactly — the production handlers registered by `startProcess` receive real stream `error` events and the real close/finalize lifecycle runs to completion.

## Regression Test Plan

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/sandbox-exec-server/processes.stream-errors.test.ts` — 2/2 passed
- `oxlint` — exit 0; `oxfmt --check` — clean

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Preserve `fs.glob` explicit directory-symlink parity: descend a symlink only when its aligned pattern segment is literal (non-wildcard) and `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace root, so an explicit configured pattern like `linked/**/AGENTS.md` still reaches descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink. Symlinks reached through a wildcard segment stay terminal (matching `fs.glob`), workspace containment rejects symlink targets that escape the root, and a `realpath` ancestor-chain guard refuses re-entry into a directory already on the descent path so an ancestor-pointing symlink (`a/loop -> a`) cannot loop.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — explicit directory-symlink glob parity across three states (real `fs.symlink`): a literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

### Directory-symlink glob parity proof

- **Behavior addressed**: The cooperative walker only descended `Dirent.isDirectory()` entries and emitted symlinks as leaf candidates, so an explicit configured pattern such as `linked/**/AGENTS.md` no longer reached descendants when `linked` is an in-workspace directory symlink — Node's `fs.glob` resolves that case, so the walker silently dropped configured bootstrap context. The walker now descends a literal-named path-segment symlink when `realpath` confirms a directory inside the workspace, keeps wildcard-reached symlinks terminal, and guards against ancestor cycles.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`. Three regression tests build real temp directories with real `fs.symlink` links and drive the real exported extra-bootstrap glob resolver.
- **Steps run**: `npx vitest run src/agents/workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts src/agents/workspace.test.ts`
- **Observed result**: `Test Files 4 passed (4)`, `Tests 156 passed (156)`. The three symlink states are covered: (a) literal-named directory symlink is descended and its descendants match; (b) a `**`-reached symlink stays terminal; (c) an ancestor-pointing (cyclic) literal symlink terminates without looping (guarded by a 15s timeout). A TDD red check confirmed test (a) fails on the pre-fix walker (missing the `linked/` descendants) and passes after the fix; `tsgo:core` exits 0 and `oxfmt --check` reports both files formatted.
- **What was not tested**: Behavior on Windows/`EPERM`/`ENOSYS` filesystems where symlink creation is unavailable — those cases skip cleanly rather than assert.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix(memory): skip blank search provider bootstrap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Memory search handled blank or whitespace-only queries too late. The manager could initialize the provider, assert provider state, or bootstrap search work before the preflight returned an empty result.

## Why This Change Was Made

Blank query eligibility is a local preflight contract and should not require provider setup. This change shares query normalization with the existing preflight and short-circuits blank queries before provider/bootstrap work.

## User Impact

Whitespace-only memory searches return `[]` cheaply and deterministically, without requiring provider credentials, indexes, or search startup.

## Evidence

- Changed `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager.ts`.
- Changed `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search-preflight.ts`.
- Added `extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager.blank-query.test.ts` proving blank search returns `[]` before provider init, provider assertion, index check, or sync bootstrap.
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-memory.config.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager-search-preflight.test.ts extensions/memory-core/src/memory/manager.blank-query.test.ts --reporter=verbose`
- `git diff --check upstream/main..HEAD`
- Controlled manager proof: `node --import tsx - <<'EOF' ...` invoked the actual `MemoryIndexManager.search` method with a whitespace-only query and provider/bootstrap counters.
- Normal manager proof: `node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'EOF' ...` constructed a real `MemoryIndexManager` through `MemoryIndexManager.get({ cfg, agentId: "main", purpose: "cli" })`, then ran a whitespace-only search.

## Proof

- Controlled proof query: whitespace-only.
- Controlled proof result: `resultCount: 0`, `results: []`.
- Provider/bootstrap counters all stayed zero: `ensureProviderInitialized: 0`, `assertRequiredProviderAvailable: 0`, `hasIndexedContent: 0`, `sync: 0`.
- Normal manager proof used a temporary workspace/state dir and `provider: "none"` with vector disabled to avoid external provider setup.
- Normal manager proof output:
  - `managerConstructed: true`
  - `purpose: "cli"`
  - `blankResultCount: 0`, `blankResults: []`
  - `beforeProviderState` and `afterProviderState`: `{ "mode": "pending", "requestedProvider": "none" }`
  - `beforeFiles: 0`, `afterFiles: 0`, `beforeChunks: 0`, `afterChunks: 0`
- This proves the blank-query preflight returns before provider initialization, provider availability assertion, index checks, or sync bootstrap on both the direct search method and a normally constructed manager path.


## Public CLI Proof

- Public CLI proof command: `pnpm openclaw memory search --query <whitespace> --json`, with `<whitespace>` equal to `" \n\t "` in a temporary `OPENCLAW_HOME`, `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, and workspace.
- Config used `agents.defaults.memorySearch.provider: "none"`, `store.vector.enabled: false`, and search/index watchers disabled, so a blank-query preflight must not need any embedding provider.
- Search exit: `0`.
- Search stdout:
  ```json
  {
    "results": []
  }
  ```
- Follow-up status command: `pnpm openclaw memory status --json` in the same fixture.
- Follow-up status core: `provider: "none"`, `requestedProvider: "none"`, `vector.enabled: false`, `files: 0`, `chunks: 0`, `dirty: true`.
- Workspace contents stayed `MEMORY.md` plus `memory/`; only the normal OpenClaw state SQLite files were created under the temporary state dir.
- This proves the public `openclaw memory search` path returns `[]` for a whitespace-only query before provider/bootstrap/index work.

target.title: fix(browser): apply profile proxy policy to tab list redaction
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
`/tabs` and `/tabs/action` list redaction only used the global SSRF policy. They did not include the selected profile's browser proxy mode, while tab open/focus/select already use `browserNavigationPolicyForProfile`.

## Why This Change Was Made
Strict browser navigation policy depends on whether the browser profile itself is proxy-routed. Tab list URL redaction is a navigation-result policy check, so it should receive the same profile-aware policy as the other tab routes.

## User Impact
Tab list responses now redact URLs consistently for proxy-routed browser profiles instead of evaluating them with an incomplete policy. This keeps list responses aligned with focus/select safety checks.

## Evidence
- Changed tab list redaction to accept `browserNavigationPolicyForProfile(ctx, profileCtx)`.
- Added route regression coverage for both `/tabs` and `/tabs/action list` passing `explicit-browser-proxy` into result guards.
- Added attach-only route proof in `extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.attach-only.test.ts` that uses the real browser route context and real navigation guard: strict SSRF plus `--proxy-server=...` redacts a public IP-literal tab URL for both list endpoints.
- Focused tests:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.attach-only.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose`
  - Result: 2 files / 24 tests passed.
- Touched-file checks:
  - `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.attach-only.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/routes/tabs.test.ts`

target.title: fix(workboard): check active claim before dependency status guard in claim()
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #104050 — `claim()` checks the dependency status guard (card status must be `"ready"`) before checking whether the card is already claimed. Since a successful claim moves the card to `"running"`, any repeat claim on a card with parents returns the misleading error `"card dependencies are not done"` instead of `"card already claimed by <owner>"`.

Cards without parents are unaffected — only the misordered dependency guard triggers this false error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Swap the order of two guards in `claim()`: check the active claim lease before the dependency status guard. The existing claim check (`already claimed by`) and dependency check (`dependencies are not done`) each remain correct on their own; the fix is purely about which one runs first.

No status transitions, no new error messages, no API changes — just moving `existingClaim` above `cardParentIds`.

**Test correction (`fbb9293dc5`):** the regression test first pushed here built the parent link through raw `metadata.links`, which `create()` strips (parent/child dependencies must go through `linkCards`). The child was therefore parentless, the dependency guard never fired, and the test passed with *or* without the fix. It now builds a real dependency via `linkCards` + `promoteReady` and asserts the link and promotion, so it genuinely guards the ordering (fails pre-fix, passes post-fix).

## User Impact

Agents that repeat-claim a dependency-backed card now see the correct `"already claimed by <owner>"` error instead of a misleading `"dependencies not done"` that sends them into dependency-debugging loops.

## Evidence

### Real runtime behavior (SQLite-backed `WorkboardStore`)

Reproduced #104050 end-to-end against a real `node:sqlite` store (not the in-memory test double), driving the public store API — build a parent→child dependency with `linkCards`, mark the parent `done`, `promoteReady`, then claim the child twice. `before` = pre-fix (`HEAD~1`), `after` = this fix.

```
########## BEFORE (pre-fix) ##########
setup   child.parents=[<cardId>] child.status=ready
claim#1 owner=main   -> status=running  token=<redacted>
claim#2 owner=other  -> Error: card dependencies are not done.     # misleading

########## AFTER (this fix) ##########
setup   child.parents=[<cardId>] child.status=ready
claim#1 owner=main   -> status=running  token=<redacted>
claim#2 owner=other  -> Error: card already claimed by main.       # correct
```

<details><summary>Repro driver (throwaway, not committed)</summary>

```ts
import { mkdtempSync } from "node:fs";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import { join } from "node:path";
import { WorkboardStore } from "./extensions/workboard/src/store.ts";
import { createWorkboardSqliteStores } from "./extensions/workboard/src/sqlite-store.ts";

const s = createWorkboardSqliteStores({
  dbPath: join(mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "wb-")), "workboard.sqlite"),
});
const store = new WorkboardStore(s.cards, {
  boards: s.boards, subscriptions: s.subscriptions, attachments: s.attachments,
});

const parent = await store.create({ title: "Parent A", status: "todo" });
const child  = await store.create({ title: "Child B",  status: "todo" });
await store.linkCards(parent.id, child.id);          // real parent->child dependency
await store.update(parent.id, { status: "done" });
await store.promoteReady();                          // child -> ready

const first = await store.claim(child.id, { ownerId: "main", ttlSeconds: 60 });
console.log("claim#1 ->", first.card.status);        // running
try { await store.claim(child.id, { ownerId: "other" }); }
catch (e) { console.log("claim#2 ->", e.message); }
```

</details>

### Regression test (now effective)

The corrected test fails on the pre-fix guard order and passes after the fix:

```
# new test @ FIXED store.ts
  Tests  1 passed

# new test @ PRE-FIX store.ts (HEAD~1)
  × reports already claimed instead of dependency error for a claimed dependency-backed card
  AssertionError: expected [Function] to throw error matching /already claimed/
    but got 'card dependencies are not done.'
```

### Full suite + lint

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/workboard/src/store.test.ts
  Test Files  1 passed (1)
       Tests  80 passed (80)

$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/workboard/src/store.ts extensions/workboard/src/store.test.ts
  exit 0
```

1 production line moved + 1 effective regression test. Bounded to `extensions/workboard/src/`. No config, SDK, CLI, docs, or changelog surface was added.

target.title: fix(web-media): add timeoutMs option to WebMediaOptions for remote fetches
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadWebMedia` / `readRemoteMediaBuffer` had no upper bound on header-arrival latency. An unresponsive upstream could pin a Tlon media download or URL-backed image upload at the TCP/streaming-read layer until `readIdleTimeoutMs` finally tripped — and only if a body ever started. This PR threads a 15-minute header-arrival deadline through `WebMediaOptions` and the two Tlon call sites so a never-responding endpoint fails fast while slow-but-progressing transfers keep going.

## Why This Change Was Made

The initial proposal exposed a new `WebMediaOptions.timeoutMs?: number` (overall-request lifetime). ClawSweeper correctly rejected that as compatibility-breaking: it would have capped healthy bodies that keep yielding past 15 minutes. The narrower `FetchMediaOptions.responseHeaderTimeoutMs` seam landed on `origin/main` via PR #103020 (merge commit `26aef8c48bc40d2ea456c2cfc3eca126dca33888`, 2026-07-10 13:31 UTC, currently reachable from `origin/main@bb26753705`) specifically for this stall class — header-only deadline via `buildTimeoutAbortSignal`, `cleanup()`-ed once headers arrive so the body is not capped. This PR drops the parallel total-timeout surface and adopts that canonical seam end-to-end.

## What Changed

- `src/media/web-media.ts` — `WebMediaOptions.timeoutMs?: number` removed; replaced with `WebMediaOptions.responseHeaderTimeoutMs?: number`. `loadWebMediaInternal` destructures the new field and forwards it conditionally into `readRemoteMediaBuffer({ ..., responseHeaderTimeoutMs })` so an unset value does not overwrite main's "no header deadline" default.
- `src/media/web-media.test.ts` — replaces the prior "aborts a … via the overall timeoutMs deadline" test with **"forwards responseHeaderTimeoutMs from loadWebMediaRaw through readRemoteMediaBuffer"** (using `vi.useFakeTimers()` + a progressing body stream, identical to main's `fetch.test.ts:438-485` "clears the response-header deadline while a healthy body keeps progressing" pattern). Asserts the resolved buffer contains the enqueued bytes after the header deadline clears — proving the public seam actually forwards the field.
- `extensions/tlon/src/monitor/media.ts` — replaces `TLON_MEDIA_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS` with `TLON_MEDIA_DOWNLOAD_RESPONSE_HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS = 15 * 60_000`; `downloadMedia`'s `fetchOptions` now forwards `responseHeaderTimeoutMs:` to both `saveRemoteMedia` and `readRemoteMediaBuffer`.
- `extensions/tlon/src/urbit/upload.ts` — replaces `TLON_UPLOAD_IMAGE_TIMEOUT_MS` with `TLON_UPLOAD_IMAGE_RESPONSE_HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS = 15 * 60_000`; `uploadImageFromUrl`'s `readRemoteMediaBuffer` call forwards the same.
- `extensions/tlon/src/monitor/media.test.ts`, `extensions/tlon/src/urbit/upload.test.ts` — assertion relaxed to `expect.objectContaining({ ..., responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 15 * 60_000 })`.
- `proof-103206-tool-run.mts` — new live-run proof that exercises the canonical seam end-to-end (real stalled HTTP server + real `loadWebMedia` + real AbortSignal + surfaced error shape).

## User Impact

- Hard 15-minute upper bound on header-arrival latency for Tlon media downloads and URL-backed image uploads triggered by `extensions/tlon`.
- Healthy upstreams see no behavior change. **Slow-but-progressing transfers are explicitly NOT capped** — once headers arrive, the header deadline is cleared and `readIdleTimeoutMs` (30s for Tlon) continues to bound chunk gaps. This is the deliberate behavior change vs. the prior total-timeout proposal.
- Tlon users on very slow networks where headers legitimately take >15 min will see new failures. This matches the existing 15-minute ceiling from canonical precedent #103266 (`src/cli/nodes-camera.ts:20`, `CAMERA_URL_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS`); the trade-off has already been accepted by maintainers on that merge.

## Evidence

### Live behavior proof (real HTTP server, real fetch, real AbortSignal, surfaced error shape)

Local fallback run (Crabbox unavailable in this env):

```
$ node node_modules/.bin/tsx proof-103206-tool-run.mts
[proof] stalled HTTP server listening on http://127.0.0.1:36539
[proof] calling loadWebMedia with responseHeaderTimeoutMs=1000ms (production code path uses 15*60_000)
[proof] this exercises the canonical seam from PR #103020:
[proof]   loadWebMedia -> readRemoteMediaBuffer -> fetchGuardedMediaResponse
[proof]   -> fetchWithSsrFGuard -> buildTimeoutAbortSignal (response header deadline)
[proof]   -> globalThis.fetch
[fetch-timeout] fetch timeout after 1000ms (elapsed 1001ms) operation=media response headers url=http://127.0.0.1:36539/never-responds.png
[proof] elapsed: 1154ms
[proof] surfaced error.name: MediaFetchError
[proof] surfaced error.code: fetch_failed
[proof] surfaced error.message: Failed to fetch media from http://127.0.0.1:36539/never-responds.png: request timed out
[proof] surfaced error.cause.name: TimeoutError
[proof] surfaced error.cause.message: request timed out
[proof] result: responseHeaderTimeoutMs fired through real production path
{
  "url": "http://127.0.0.1:36539/never-responds.png",
  "responseHeaderTimeoutMs": 1000,
  "outcome": {
    "kind": "error",
    "name": "MediaFetchError",
    "code": "fetch_failed",
    "message": "Failed to fetch media from http://127.0.0.1:36539/never-responds.png: request timed out",
    "causeName": "TimeoutError",
    "causeMessage": "request timed out",
    "elapsedMs": 1154
  },
  "passed": true
}
```

Key observations:
- **1154ms elapsed** (vs 1000ms `responseHeaderTimeoutMs`): the `[fetch-timeout]` log fires at the deadline, proving the AbortSignal fires at the configured header deadline.
- **Surfaced error shape**: `MediaFetchError { code: "fetch_failed", cause: TimeoutError("request timed out") }` — the exact error shape that propagates to the Tlon extension caller.

### Repository test (forwards responseHeaderTimeoutMs through the public seam)

Added in `src/media/web-media.test.ts > loadWebMedia > forwards responseHeaderTimeoutMs from loadWebMediaRaw through readRemoteMediaBuffer`. The test uses `vi.useFakeTimers()` and an `enqueue([1],25) → enqueue([2],50) → close(75)` body stream (matching main's pattern at `fetch.test.ts:438-485`). Asserts the resolved buffer equals the concatenation of enqueued bytes — proving the header deadline is cleared on success and the body keeps progressing past it.

Focused suite runs (local fallback — Crabbox unavailable in this env):

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/media/web-media.test.ts src/media/fetch.test.ts --reporter=verbose
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  121 passed (121)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/tlon/src/monitor/media.test.ts extensions/tlon/src/urbit/upload.test.ts --reporter=verbose
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  11 passed (11)
```

target.title: fix(shell): resolve pwsh.exe/.cmd/.bat on PATH for Windows shell discovery
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

On Windows, PowerShell 7 delivered via the Microsoft Store / App Execution Alias (and most portable installs) ships as `pwsh.exe`. `resolvePowerShellPath()` step 3 calls `resolveShellFromPath("pwsh")`, which only probed a **bare** `pwsh` with no extension. `fs.accessSync(entry/pwsh)` therefore returned `ENOENT`, so shell discovery fell through to Windows PowerShell 5.1 instead of using pwsh 7. This is the actual Windows pwsh resolution gap (distinct from the custom-shell `-c` args discussion in #104053).

## Evidence

Local reproduction on this Windows host (PowerShell 7.6.3 present only as the Store `pwsh.exe` alias, no `C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7`):
- `fs.accessSync("...\pwsh")` -> `ENOENT` (bare name missed by discovery)
- `fs.accessSync("...\pwsh.exe")` -> `OK` (extension probe hits it)
- After the fix, `resolveShellFromPath("pwsh")` returns the `pwsh.exe` path on PATH, and `resolvePowerShellPath()` prefers pwsh 7 over the 5.1 fallback.

This matches the source-level analysis: current main only looks for a bare `pwsh`, so a PATH entry containing only `pwsh.exe` is skipped before the Windows PowerShell 5.1 fallback (noted by the ClawSweeper review). The PR also adds Windows-only regression tests (guarded by `isWin` so Linux CI is unaffected): finds `pwsh.exe` when a bare `pwsh` is absent, prefers a bare `pwsh` match over `pwsh.exe` when both exist, and `resolvePowerShellPath()` resolves `pwsh.exe` on PATH instead of 5.1.

(Private paths and credentials redacted; this is a local OpenClaw gateway host.)

## Root cause

`resolveShellFromPath` joined the entry with the bare name and never tried executable extensions on Windows:

```ts
const candidate = path.join(entry, name); // only "pwsh", never "pwsh.exe"
```

## Fix

On `win32`, also probe `.exe`, mirroring the existing pattern already used by `resolveWindowsBashPath` (`"bash.exe"` / `"bash"`).

```ts
const executableExtensions = process.platform === "win32" ? [".exe"] : [];
const candidates = [base, ...executableExtensions.map((ext) => base + ext)];
```

**Scope note (addressed ClawSweeper review):** only `.exe` is added. `.cmd`/`.bat` are intentionally excluded because PTY execution (`createPtyAdapter`) spawns the resolved shell directly without child mode's `cmd.exe` wrapping, so a `pwsh.cmd` selected here could be chosen and then fail in PTY mode. `.exe` is directly executable in both child and PTY modes. Non-Windows behavior is unchanged.

This makes a Store/portable `pwsh.exe` discoverable on PATH, so `resolvePowerShellPath()` prefers pwsh 7 over 5.1.

## Test plan

Windows-only tests in `shell-utils.test.ts` (guarded by `isWin` so Linux CI is unaffected):
- finds `pwsh.exe` when a bare `pwsh` is absent
- prefers a bare `pwsh` match over `pwsh.exe` when both exist
- `resolvePowerShellPath()` resolves `pwsh.exe` on PATH instead of 5.1 when standard install dirs are empty

Existing tests unchanged; non-Windows `resolveShellFromPath` behavior preserved.

target.title: fix(codex): trigger model fallback on usage-limit promptError (#103734)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a Codex-backed turn hits the subscription usage limit, the Codex harness
returns a `promptError` in the attempt result instead of throwing. The host's
model fallback is throw-driven — it only engages when `FailoverError` is thrown.

The existing prompt-error handler already classifies the error and enters
`resolveRunFailoverDecision`.  However `shouldRotatePrompt` always returns true
for rate/billing limits, so the handler first tries **auth profile rotation** —
retrying the same harness with a different profile.  For harness-owned transports
(Codex) the limit is on the harness session, not the profile, so every rotation
fails identically.  This wastes the user's quota and burns retry budget
before fallback can engage.

Fixes #103734.

## Why This Change Was Made

One 8-line addition in `shouldRotatePrompt` (`failover-policy.ts`): when a
plugin harness owns the transport **and** the failover reason is `rate_limit`
or `billing`, skip profile rotation.  The decision falls through to
`fallback_model` in `resolveRunFailoverDecision`, which throws a `FailoverError`
that the outer fallback loop catches immediately.

Non-harness providers and non-limit errors are unchanged — they still rotate
profiles before falling back.

## User Impact

**Before:** Codex usage limit → profile rotation → all profiles fail →
run budget exhausted or model fallback with wasted quota.

**After:** Codex usage limit → `rate_limit` → skips rotation → falls back
to next configured model immediately.

## Evidence

### Live agent proof (Codex usage-limit → fallback model)

Primary `openai/gpt-5.5` (Codex) forced to return a redacted usage-limit error.
Fallback `zte/Qwen3-235B-A22B` configured.  Run completes on the fallback:

```
$ pnpm --filter openclaw openclaw agent --local \
    --message "say hello in one word" --session-key agent:proof:103734

# (1) Codex turn fails with usage-limit → decision=fallback_model
[agent/embedded] embedded run failover decision:
  stage=prompt decision=fallback_model reason=rate_limit
  from=openai/gpt-5.5

# (2) FailoverError thrown → model fallback loop catches it
[diagnostic] lane task error: FailoverError: You've reached your Codex
  subscription usage limit.

# (3) Fallback switches to zte/Qwen3-235B-A22B
[model-fallback/decision] decision=candidate_failed
  candidate=openai/gpt-5.5 reason=rate_limit
  next=zte/Qwen3-235B-A22B

# (4) Fallback model succeeds
[provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response
  provider=zte model=Qwen3-235B-A22B status=200

[model-fallback/decision] decision=candidate_succeeded
  candidate=zte/Qwen3-235B-A22B

Hello

[agent] run ended with stopReason=stop
```

✅ Codex usage-limit → `fallback_model` (no profile rotation) → ZTE succeeds.

### Decision policy proof script

```
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof/codex-usage-limit-fallback.mts

Step 1 — classify usage-limit → rate_limit: PASS
Step 2 — harness-owned rate_limit → fallback_model: PASS
Step 3 — harness-owned billing → fallback_model: PASS
Step 4 — harness-owned server_error → rotate_profile: PASS

OVERALL: ALL PASSED
```

target.title: fix(agents): add size limit to LSP message parser
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: The LSP message parser accepted unbounded `Content-Length`
values. A malicious or misbehaving LSP server could send an arbitrarily
large `Content-Length` header, causing unbounded buffer allocation and
memory exhaustion. Additionally, a very long decimal `Content-Length`
(e.g., 400+ digits) causes `Number.parseInt` to return `Infinity`, which
was stored as an infinite drain counter — permanently suppressing all
future LSP output and leaving pending requests to time out.

**Root cause**: When `Content-Length` exceeded the 10 MB limit, the parser
only skipped the header + separator bytes but kept the declared body in
`session.buffer`. If the oversized body arrived across multiple stream
chunks, the buffer would grow unboundedly. For non-safe integer lengths
(`Infinity` from `parseInt`), the arithmetic computed `bodyStart + Infinity
= Infinity`, storing an infinite `oversizeDrainRemaining` that never
decrements. Additionally, when the final drain chunk exactly matched the
remaining byte count, the handler returned early without failing the
session, leaving the pending request to time out.

**Solution**: Add a 10 MB `Content-Length` limit that fully drains the
declared oversized body when the frame is completely buffered, or tracks
remaining bytes to skip via `session.oversizeDrainRemaining` when the body
arrives across chunks. Non-safe integer Content-Length values (Infinity)
are detected before drain arithmetic and signal a fatal protocol error.
Finite oversized frames (>10 MB but still a safe integer) trigger session
failure after dispatching any valid responses parsed before the oversized
frame — the associated pending request is rejected immediately instead of
waiting for the normal request timeout. The exact-match drain completion
boundary (`raw.length === oversizeDrainRemaining`) now falls through to
the session failure check instead of returning early.

**What changed**: `src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.ts`
- `parseLspMessages`: accepts optional `oversizeDrainRemaining` out-param
  with `fatal` flag; on oversized frames drains the full frame or signals
  remaining bytes and sets the fatal flag. On non-safe integer
  Content-Length signals a fatal condition via NaN.
- `handleIncomingData`: drains `session.oversizeDrainRemaining` from raw
  stream data before appending to the parse buffer. Detects non-finite
  drain remaining or drained finite oversized frames and calls
  `failLspSession` after dispatching any completed responses parsed
  before the bad header. Fixed the exact-match drain boundary: changed
  `<=` to `<` so the exact-match case continues into session failure.
- `LspSession` type: added `oversizeDrainRemaining: number`,
  `oversizeDrainSeen: boolean`

**What did NOT change**: Valid message parsing, session lifecycle, tool
materialization — all unchanged for frames within the 10 MB limit.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: LSP message parser now closes three gaps:
1) fully drains finite oversized Content-Length frames (>10 MB) to
prevent memory exhaustion, 2) fails the session for non-safe integer
Content-Length (Infinity from parseInt) instead of permanently suppressing
all future LSP output, and 3) fails the session for finite oversized
frames after dispatching any valid responses parsed before the oversized
frame so the associated pending request is rejected immediately instead
of timing out.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 4.19.112, Node 22.19.0, pnpm 11.2.2

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
pnpm test src/agents/agent-bundle-lsp-runtime.test.ts
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All 18 tests pass, including 4 new
handler-level tests for finite oversized Content-Length session failure.

**Before-fix behavior (if applicable)**: Finite oversized frames (>10 MB)
were silently drained without failing the session, leaving the associated
pending request to time out after 10 seconds instead of failing
immediately. When the final drain chunk exactly matched the remaining
oversized body bytes, the handler returned early with a zero counter
without failing the session.

**After-fix evidence**:

All 18 tests pass:
```text
 ✓ bundle LSP runtime > oversized Content-Length handling (2)
 ✓ bundle LSP runtime > unsafe Content-Length handling (4)
 ✓ bundle LSP runtime > finite oversized Content-Length handling (4)
   ✓ sets fatal flag on parseLspMessages oversizeDrain
   ✓ fails LSP session on finite oversized frame through runtime handler path
   ✓ dispatches valid response before failing session on finite oversized frame
   ✓ fails the session when the final drain chunk exactly completes
```

**Real LSP server evidence**:

Tested against `vscode-json-languageserver` via stdio:

**Terminal output**:
```text
============================================================
L2 EVIDENCE: Real LSP server session via Content-Length framing
Server: vscode-json-languageserver
============================================================
Frame #1: {
  "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 1,
  "result": {
    "capabilities": {
      "textDocumentSync": 2, "hoverProvider": true,
      "documentSymbolProvider": true, "foldingRangeProvider": true,
      "selectionRangeProvider": true
    }
  }
}
Frame #2: { "jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": 2, "result": null }
----------------------------------------
Initialize returned capabilities: ✅
Completion responded: ✅
CONCLUSION: Real LSP server session works end-to-end ✅
```

This proves the LSP message parser correctly handles real server I/O
with proper Content-Length framing.

**What was not tested**: A real LSP server sending non-safe Content-Length
or oversized (>10 MB) values — these are protocol violations that no
well-behaved LSP server would produce. The code paths are exercised
through handler-level tests that use the identical `handleIncomingData`
path the production LSP session uses.

**Risk level**: Low — non-safe and finite oversized Content-Length values
both trigger session failure after dispatching valid responses. All
existing message sizes within the 10 MB limit use the unchanged happy
path. merge-risk: low

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible — 10 MB is well above realistic LSP message sizes
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations — all 18 tests pass
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation — no docs changes needed
- [x] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary — none
